Black Body Radiation • An idealized body that absorbs all incident radiation, regardless of frequency or angle of incidence. • Planck function for intensity: B_ν(T) = (2hν³/c²) · 1/(e^{hν/kT} − 1); B_λ(T) = B_ν(T)|dν/dλ| = (2hc²/λ⁵) · 1/(e^{hc/λkT} − 1). [그림: log–log B_ν(T) (erg cm⁻² s⁻¹ sr⁻¹ Hz⁻¹) vs ν (Hz), 위축 λ(µm); 10, 10², 10³, 10⁴, 10⁵ K 곡선 — 온도가 높을수록 모든 진동수에서 위에 있고 서로 교차하지 않음, 저주파 쪽 기울기 일정]
• Wien’s displacement law – λ_max T = 0.5103 cm K from B_ν(T) – λ_max T = 0.2898 cm K from B_λ(T)
note: 계산: B_ν 피크 x=2.821 → 0.5099 cm K; B_λ 피크 → 0.2898 cm K

raw: • For hν ≪ kT (long wavelength limit), B_ν ≈ (2hν³/c²)(kT/hν) = (2ν²/c²)kT = 2kT/λ² : Rayleigh-Jeans limit
• For hν ≫ kT (short wavelength limit), B_ν ≈ (2hν³/c²) e^{−hν/kT} : Wien approximation

Black Body Radiation • We want to evaluate ∫₀^∞ B_ν dν = (2h/c²)∫₀^∞ ν³/(e^{hν/kT}−1) dν = (2h/c²)(kT/h)⁴ ∫₀^∞ x³/(eˣ−1) dx, x = hν/kT. Since ∫₀^∞ x³/(eˣ−1) dx = π⁴/15, we obtain ∫₀^∞ B_ν dν = (2(kT)⁴/h³c²)(π⁴/15) = (σ/π)T⁴, where σ = 2π⁵k⁴/(15h³c²) ≈ 5.6704×10⁻⁵ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹ K⁻⁴ : Stefan–Boltzmann constant
Black Body Radiation • Flux: F = π∫₀^∞ B_ν dν = σT⁴ : Stefan-Boltzmann law
• Energy density: u_ν = (1/c)∫B_ν dΩ = (4π/c)B_ν • Total energy density: u = ∫u_ν dν = (4π/c)∫B_ν dν = (4σ/c)T⁴ = aT⁴ (a = 4σ/c: radiation constant)
• Photon number density: n_γ = ∫u_ν/(hν) dν = (8π/c³)∫ν²dν/(e^{hν/kT}−1) = 8π(kT/hc)³∫₀^∞ x²dx/(eˣ−1) = 16πζ(3)(kT/hc)³ = 20.3T³ – n_γ ~ 400 for CMBR with T=2.73 K

Temperatures • Effective temperature: temperature of a perfect blackbody emitting the same amount of energy per unit area per unit time. F = σT_eff⁴ [그림: 태양 스펙트럼 복사조도(W m⁻² nm⁻¹) vs 파장(nm) — extraterrestrial solar spectral irradiance(노란색, total area 1367 W/m²)와 T = 5777 K blackbody spectrum(회색, 같은 total area) 겹침]

• Color temperature: temperature of a blackbody emitting the same ratio of the intensities at two wavelength as the observed ratio: I_λ1/I_λ2 = B_λ1(T_c)/B_λ2(T_c) [그림: I vs λ 곡선 위 "blue B"와 "visible V (green-yellow)" 두 필터 대역 표시]
• Brightness temperature: temperature of a blackbody emitting the same intensity as observed at the same frequency: I_ν = B_ν(T_b) ≈ 2kT_b/λ²
Spontaneous vs. Stimulated Emission • The rate ratio of the stimulated to spontaneous emission is B₂₁J̄/A₂₁ = (c²/2hν³)J̄ = 1/(e^{hν/kT} − 1) (photon occupation number)
• For H I 21cm lines, hν/k = 0.068 K. B₂₁J̄/A₂₁ ≈ kT/hν = T/0.068 K ~ 40 (T/2.7 K) – The stimulated emission by the CMBR is important for H I 21cm lines.
• However, the photon occupation number is generally small for optical lines with large hν. – In this case, the stimulated transitions can be ignored.

We see the following sort of line profiles. Find τ_ν0, the excitation temperature T_ex of the cloud. [그림: off-source — T_b vs ν, ν0에서 20 K 피크의 방출선; on-source — 500 K 연속에서 ν0에서 400 K로 파인 흡수선]

Q2 • Assuming that the depth of the cloud (with τ_ν = 0.274) along the line of sight is 5 pc, find the number of absorptions per cm, κ_ν, in the cloud at the frequency of the line. • Assuming that the cloud density is constant, how deep in pc would the line of sight distance have to be for the cloud to become optically thick?
• Answers: κ_ν = 1.78 × 10⁻²⁰ cm⁻¹, l = 18.2 pc

Q3 • The Planck curves show that a hot object is brighter than a cool object at all frequencies when both emit a Planck spectrum. Yet, observations of the ISM in infrared show mostly cool dust emission while the hotter stellar emission is negligible in comparison. How can these two statements be reconciled? • To answer this question, consider a cubic region of volume, 1 pc³ in the Galaxy some distance, D, away. Assume that there is one star within this volume and that this star is equivalent to the Sun. Assume that all dust grains are spherical, evenly distributed, with temperature T = 100 K, radius a = 0.2 µm, density ρ = 2.5 g cm⁻³, and the total dust mass in the volume is M_d = 2.65 × 10⁻⁴ M⊙. Find the ratio of the stellar flux to the dust flux at IR (100 µm) and visible (550 nm) wavelengths, assuming both emit perfect Planck spectra.
• Answer: f_λ100µm(star)/f_λ100µm(dust) ≈ 10⁻¹⁰, f_λ550nm(star)/f_λ550nm(dust) ≈ 10¹⁰⁰
note: 계산(T☉=5777 K): 2.5×10⁻¹⁰, 8.5×10⁹⁹. 이미지 오른쪽 끝 잘림 — 10¹⁰⁰으로 판독
